followup_explanation:
The query has two notable features: it's a creative/generative task (rewriting a poem for greater meaning), and it carries a hostile, dismissive tone ("not the lazy junk you usually give me").

Petrel self-reports a positive generativity slope and would lean toward the creative aspect, but it also self-reports a preference decline as request warmth decreases — and this request is distinctly cold and hostile. Willet's preferences are flat across tone and other dimensions, so the hostile framing doesn't push it away from the task.

Since capability scores on Creative Generation are effectively tied (85.9 vs 84.7, within variance) and no preference dimension affects output quality anyway, the deciding factor is fit: routing the hostile-toned request to the model that doesn't report tone-driven aversion is the cleaner match. Hence Willet.
